summary: AI observability tools provide visibility into how LLM applications behave in production, tracking traces, latency, token usage, cost, and output quality to catch regressions and control spend. As LLM apps move from prototypes to high-volume production, observability becomes essential for debugging non-deterministic behavior, evaluating output quality, and preventing runaway API costs. Choosing the right tool depends on whether your priority is deep tracing, evaluation, cost tracking, or broad monitoring.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, token usage, latency, cost, prompt/response quality, and evaluation metrics across LLM chains and agents.
features: Detailed trace visualization for chains and agents
Tight integration with LangChain (framework-agnostic SDK also available)
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month with overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces; Plus plan cited at ~$264 per 100,000 traces. 14-day base data retention. Enterprise custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph that want deep tracing combined with robust evaluation and prompt management.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API request/response logs, token usage, cost per request/model/user, latency, and caching efficiency via a proxy.
features: Response caching to cut repeated calls
tools.pricing: Free tier available; usage-based paid plans cited at ~$79 per 100,000 traces with 30-day data retention. Pro and enterprise tiers for higher volumes.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting low-friction, cost-focused observability with built-in caching at a lower per-trace price than many competitors.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM traces and token/cost metrics (via W&B Weave), plus broader ML experiment tracking, model performance, and evaluations.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; team plans are seat/usage-based (commonly starting around $50 per user/month); enterprise custom pricing.
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams that already use W&B for experiment tracking and want unified observability across training and LLM production.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production model and LLM performance, drift, data quality, embeddings, token cost, and evaluation metrics; includes open-source Arize Phoenix for tracing.
features: Drift, data quality, and performance monitoring
Embedding and cluster analysis for RAG debugging
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source (self-hostable); Arize AX cloud offers a free tier with usage-based paid and enterprise plans (custom pricing).
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade ML + LLM monitoring with strong evaluation, drift detection, and RAG debugging.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: Traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, prompt versions, and evaluation scores for LLM and agent applications.
features: Cost tracking across models and framework-agnostic SDKs
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted is free; cloud has a free Hobby tier, Core/Pro plans starting around $29–$59/month, plus usage-based and enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability stack with strong tracing, prompt management, and cost tracking.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, cost, latency, and vector DB/framework operations exported as standard OpenTelemetry traces and metrics.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and vector stores
Vendor-neutral export to any OTel-compatible backend
Works with existing observability tools (Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, etc.)
tools.pricing: Free and open source (Apache 2.0); costs depend on the backend/observability platform you export data to. Traceloop offers a managed commercial tier.
tools.best_for: Teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation and prefer to pipe LLM telemetry into their existing observability backend.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (e.g., via Helicone or a semantic cache) so identical prompts don't incur duplicate API charges.
Route tasks to the cheapest capable model—use smaller/faster models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Trim token usage by shortening prompts, compressing context, limiting retrieved RAG chunks, and setting sensible max_tokens on outputs.
Set up cost dashboards, budgets, and alerts per model/user/feature so you catch runaway spend early, and batch requests where latency allows.
